text_en: When it was decided that we were to sail for Italy, they transferred Paul and some other prisoners to a centurion of the Augustan Cohort, named Julius.
text_cn: 既决定了要我们坐船往意大利去，人就将保禄和一些别的囚犯，交给皇家营里的一个百夫长，他名叫犹里约。

text_en: Embarking on a ship of Adramyttium that was about to set sail to the ports along the coast of Asia, we put to sea, accompanied by Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica.
text_cn: 有一只由阿得辣米特来的船，要开往亚细亚沿岸一带地方去。我们上去，便开了船，同我们一起的，还有马其顿的得撒洛尼人阿黎斯塔苛。

text_en: The next day we put in at Sidon; and Julius treated Paul kindly, and allowed him to go to his friends to be cared for.
text_cn: 第二天，我们在漆冬靠了岸，犹里约优待保禄，准他到朋友那里去获得照应。

text_en: Putting out to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were against us.
text_cn: 我们又从那里开了船，因为是逆风，便沿塞浦路斯背风的海面航行，

text_en: After we had sailed across the sea that is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra in Lycia.
text_cn: 横渡基里基雅和旁非里雅一带的海面，便到了里基雅的米辣。

text_en: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship bound for Italy and put us on board.
text_cn: 百夫长在那里找到一只由亚历山大里亚来，要开往意大利的船，便叫我们上了那船。

text_en: We sailed slowly for a number of days and arrived with difficulty off Cnidus, and as the wind was against us, we sailed under the lee of Crete off Salmone.
text_cn: 我们一连多日缓慢航行，仅到了克尼多对面，因为风阻止我们，我们就靠着克里特背风的海面，在撒耳摩讷旁边航行，

text_en: Sailing past it with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.
text_cn: 我们沿岸而行，方才来到一个名叫良港的地方，拉撒雅城就在附近。

text_en: Since much time had been lost and sailing was now dangerous, because even the Fast had already gone by, Paul advised them,
text_cn: 历时既久，航海已很危险，因为禁食节已过了， 保禄就劝告他们说：

text_en: saying, “Sirs, I can see that the voyage will be with danger and much heavy loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives. ”
text_cn: “诸位同人！我看这次航行，不但货物和船，就是连我们的性命，也将要遭受灾害和重大的损失。”

text_en: But the centurion paid more attention to the pilot and to the owner of the ship than to what Paul said.
text_cn: 可是，百夫长宁信从舵手和船主，不听保禄所说的话。

text_en: Since the harbor was not suitable for spending the winter, the majority was in favor of putting to sea from there, on the chance that somehow they could reach Phoenix, where they could spend the winter. It was a harbor of Crete, facing southwest and northwest.
text_cn: 又因为这港口不适于过冬，大多数人便提议由这里开船，或者能到腓尼斯去过冬，腓尼斯是克里特的一个港口，面朝西南和西北。

text_en: When a moderate south wind began to blow, they thought they could achieve their purpose; so they weighed anchor and began to sail past Crete, close to the shore.
text_cn: 那时，南风徐徐吹来，大家以为对目的地已有了把握，就启锚沿着克里特航行。

text_en: But soon a violent wind, called the northeaster, rushed down from Crete.
text_cn: 可是，过了不久，有一种称为“东北风”的飓风，向岛上冲来。

text_en: Since the ship was caught and could not be turned head-on into the wind, we gave way to it and were driven.
text_cn: 船被飓风卷去，不能顶风而行，我们只好任风飘流。

text_en: By running under the lee of a small island called Cauda we were scarcely able to get the ship’s boat under control.
text_cn: 当我们贴着一个名叫克劳达小岛的背风处疾驶时，才能将小艇把持住，

text_en: After hoisting it up they took measures to undergird the ship; then, fearing that they would run on the Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and so were driven.
text_cn: 水手们把小艇拉上来，用缆索把船绑好、又怕撞在叙尔提浅滩上，便落下船具，这样任船飘荡。

text_en: We were being pounded by the storm so violently that on the next day they began to throw the cargo overboard,
text_cn: 我们被风浪巅簸得太厉害，第二天他们便将货物抛去；

text_en: and on the third day with their own hands they threw the ship’s tackle overboard.
text_cn: 第三天他们又亲手把船上的用具也抛弃了。

text_en: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and no small tempest raged, all hope of our being saved was at last abandoned.
text_cn: 好多天看不见太阳，看不见星辰，狂暴的风仍不见小，从此我们获救的希望，全都消失了。

text_en: Since they had been without food for a long time, Paul then stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have listened to me and not have set sail from Crete and thereby avoided this damage and loss.
text_cn: 众人好久已没有吃饭，保禄便站在他们中间说：“诸位同人，你们本该听我的话，不该从克里特开船，而遭受这场灾害和损失。

text_en: I urge you now to keep up your courage, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
text_cn: 虽然如此，我现在仍劝你们放心，因为除这只船外，你们中没有一个会丧命的，

text_en: For last night there stood by me an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I worship,
text_cn: 因为，我所归属和所事奉的天主的使者，今夜曾显现给我，

text_en: and he said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before the emperor; and indeed, God has granted safety to all those who are sailing with you. ’
text_cn: 说：保禄！不要害怕，你必要站在凯撒面前。看，一切和你同船的人，天主都已赐给你了。

text_en: So keep up your courage, men, for I have faith in God that it will be exactly as I have been told.
text_cn: 因此，诸位同人！请放心好了，因为我信天主对我怎样说，也必怎样成就；

text_en: But we will have to run aground on some island. ”
text_cn: 不过我们必要搁浅在一个岛上。”

text_en: When the fourteenth night had come, as we were drifting across the sea of Adria, about midnight the sailors suspected that they were nearing land.
text_cn: 到了第十四天夜里，我们在亚得里亚海飘来飘去； 约在半夜时分，水手们猜想离一处陆地近了，

text_en: So they took soundings and found twenty fathoms; a little farther on they took soundings again and found fifteen fathoms.
text_cn: 便抛下测铅，得知水深二十寻；隔了一会，又抛下测铅，得知水深十五寻。

text_en: Fearing that we might run on the rocks, they let down four anchors from the stern and prayed for day to come.
text_cn: 他们又怕我们碰在礁石上，就从船尾抛下四个锚，切望天亮。

text_en: But when the sailors tried to escape from the ship and had lowered the boat into the sea, on the pretext of putting out anchors from the bow,
text_cn: 水手想法离船逃走，便将小艇系到海里，假装要从船头抛锚的样子，

text_en: Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men stay in the ship, you cannot be saved. ”
text_cn: 保禄就给百夫长和士兵说：“这些人若不留在船上，你们便不能获救。”

text_en: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat and set it adrift.
text_cn: 那时，士兵便割断小艇的缆索，任它沉没。

text_en: Just before daybreak, Paul urged all of them to take some food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day that you have been in suspense and remaining without food, having eaten nothing.
text_cn: 从那时直到天亮，保禄一直劝众人用饭说：“你们一直忍饥期待，没有吃什么，到今天已是第十四天了。

text_en: Therefore I urge you to take some food, for it will help you survive; for none of you will lose a hair from your heads. ”
text_cn: 所以我劝你们用饭；这与你们获救有关，因为连你们头上的头发也不会失掉一根。”

text_en: After he had said this, he took bread; and giving thanks to God in the presence of all, he broke it and began to eat.
text_cn: 保禄说了这话，便拿起饼来，在众人前，感谢了天主，然后擘开，开始吃。

text_en: Then all of them were encouraged and took food for themselves.
text_cn: 于是众人都放了心，也都用了饭。

text_en: (We were in all two hundred seventy-six persons in the ship. )
text_cn: 当时我们在船上的，共有二百七十六人。

text_en: After they had satisfied their hunger, they lightened the ship by throwing the wheat into the sea.
text_cn: 众人都吃饱了饭，便把麦子抛在海里，使船轻些。

text_en: In the morning they did not recognize the land, but they noticed a bay with a beach, on which they planned to run the ship ashore, if they could.
text_cn: 当天亮时，他们不认得那陆地，但瞥见一个有岸边的海湾，如果可能，就愿意把船驶进去。

text_en: So they cast off the anchors and left them in the sea. At the same time they loosened the ropes that tied the steering-oars; then hoisting the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.
text_cn: 于是将锚割断，弃在海里，同时松开舵绳，拉上前帆，顺着风，向岸边前进。

text_en: But striking a reef, they ran the ship aground; the bow stuck and remained immovable, but the stern was being broken up by the force of the waves.
text_cn: 不料却碰到一道沙滩，两边有海，竟把船搁浅了，船头陷入，胶定不动，船尾却被浪涛猛力冲坏。

text_en: The soldiers’ plan was to kill the prisoners, so that none might swim away and escape;
text_cn: 那时士兵主张要把囚犯杀掉，免得有人泅水逃走；

text_en: but the centurion, wishing to save Paul, kept them from carrying out their plan. He ordered those who could swim to jump overboard first and make for the land,
text_cn: 可是百夫长却愿救保禄，便阻止他们任意行事，遂命令会泅水的先跳入水中，先行登陆，

text_en: and the rest to follow, some on planks and others on pieces of the ship. And so it was that all were brought safely to land.
text_cn: 至于其余的人，有的用木板，有的凭船上的零碎东西：这样众人都登了陆，得了救。
